what: Per-test rows from NASA Physical Science Informatics (PSI) combustion investigations, one row per test.
source: NASA Physical Science Informatics, https://psi.nasa.gov/ (NASA open data). Each row names its file (source), its line in that file (source_line), the investigation page (source_url) and the raw cells used (raw).
download_method: GET https://psi.nasa.gov/geode-py/ws/repo/investigations/PSI-<n> lists files; the per-test tables are under 'experimentalTable'.
GET https://psi.nasa.gov/geode-py/ws/studies/PSI-<n>/download?file=<file_name>&redirect=false returns a short-lived link to the CSV.
generated_by: scripts/build_tests.py, written with an AI coding assistant (Claude Code). Values are copied or unit-converted from NASA's tables by code; no value was typed or estimated by AI.

conversions.oxygen: mole fractions multiplied by 100 to give o2_pct

field_notes.pressure_from: 'test' when the table gives pressure for the test; null when no pressure is stated. No investigation text states a cabin pressure for BASS, BASS-II or SAFFIRE, so those rows have pressure_psi null and are not plotted.
field_notes.oxygen_from: 'chamber' is the surrounding atmosphere. 'burner' is the oxygen stream of an inverse flame (fuel fills the chamber), which is not a cabin atmosphere: keep these off the cabin map or mark them.
field_notes.outcome: CFI-G: ignited and SE gives self_extinguished, ignited and FT (flow terminated) gives burned, no ignition gives unknown with ignited=false. FLEX: Extinction gives self_extinguished, Completion gives burned, Disruption gives unknown. SAFFIRE: a burn time in seconds gives burned; 'Insignificant' (NASA's word, four SAFFIRE-II silicone samples) gives self_extinguished. All other rows: unknown (the table records no outcome). outcome_note keeps NASA's own cell text.
field_notes.diluent: n2_pct, co2_pct and he_pct are the other gases in the chamber, as mole fractions times 100. Given only by FLEX (nitrogen, carbon dioxide, helium) and CFI (nitrogen, helium). The FLEX file drops subscripts, so its 'O', 'N' and 'CO' columns are read as O2, N2 and CO2. Missing means the table does not state it.
field_notes.burn_time_s: FLEX 'Burn time; s', CFI-G 'burn time (sec)', SAFFIRE 'Burn Time (s)'. Words and blanks give null. burn_time_approx is true where NASA wrote the time with '~' (two FLEX rows).
field_notes.pressure_approx: true for CFI-G, whose column is headed 'approx p (bar)'.
field_notes.gravity_comparison: ug_burn_length and g1_burn_length copy SAFFIRE-II's microgravity and 1 g burn length cells as text. They are the only place in these tables where NASA lists both gravity levels for one sample.
field_notes.pressure_psi: A pressure of 0 in a table (FLEX test C11M201 lists 0 mmHg) is read as not recorded and gives null.
field_notes.o2_pct: Ranges such as '21.5 - 21.7' or '22.1 to 22.0' give null; approximate values such as '~ 21.5' are kept.
field_notes.gravity: All tests ran in microgravity (ISS or the Cygnus spacecraft).
field_notes.flow_cm_s: Given only by SAFFIRE. BASS-II records a fan display setting, not a speed, so flow is null.
field_notes.exclude_reason: null for a normal test. Set only for rows that are not separate tests: a row NASA's file repeats word for word (CFI lists 8 tests twice), and a BASS log entry with no test number ('SOOT Cleaning'). These rows stay in tests.json and are left out of tests.web.json. Rows that share a test_id but differ in any cell (re-runs in FLEX and BASS) are kept as separate tests.
field_notes.test_id: Not unique: re-runs can repeat an ID. Use source plus source_line to identify a row.

files.tests.json: Full record: every row read from NASA's tables, with raw cells and provenance. Keep for checking.
files.tests.web.json: Slim copy for the website: rows with exclude_reason left out, fields limited to accession, test_id, fuel, fuel_phase, o2_pct, pressure_psi, pressure_from, flow_cm_s, gravity, outcome, source, investigation, flame_type, oxygen_from, ignited, source_line, plus n2_pct, co2_pct, he_pct, burn_time_s, burn_time_approx, outcome_note, pressure_approx, ug_burn_length, g1_burn_length on the rows where NASA's table has a value. Values identical to tests.json. Investigation page: https://psi.nasa.gov/physci/repo/data/investigations/<accession>.

excluded.PSI-20: ACME BRE: one row per test day, several oxygen values in one cell, no per-test pressure
excluded.PSI-21: ACME CLD Flame: one row per test day, fuel concentration ranges only
excluded.PSI-22: ACME E-FIELD Flames: one row per test day, no oxygen or pressure
excluded.PSI-23: ACME s-Flame: one row per test day, atmosphere as text (~21% O2)
excluded.PSI-68: FLEX-2: one row per fuel with ranges of oxygen and pressure, not per test
excluded.PSI-101: SAME-R: smoke measurement, nothing burned in a flame test
excluded.PSI-102: SAME: smoke measurement, nothing burned in a flame test
excluded.PSI-106: SLICE: test date and fuel only
excluded.PSI-107: SPICE: soot of gas jets in air; the table gives no oxygen or pressure
excluded.PSI-142: Cool flame study: list of figures in publications, not tests
excluded.PSI-60, PSI-62, PSI-115, PSI-117: analysis or ground studies with no per-test table
